subject: Surveying and fitting around business operations
hook: Evenings and weekends, or zone by zone in the working day?
ig:
Evenings and weekends, or zone by zone in the working day?

If your business is getting new furniture, this is the real choice.

A: Out of hours
The office looks normal every morning. Customers and staff never meet a fitter. The trade-off: shorter sessions on site, and your building needs to allow access, alarms and lifts after hours.

B: Phased, in hours
Longer working days mean the whole job finishes sooner. The trade-off: some areas are out of action while each zone is fitted, so people move around for a while.

Plenty of businesses mix the two: reception after hours, back-office areas during the day.

Which suits your workplace, A or B, and what kind of business are you? We'll reply with how we'd plan it.
fb:
If you run a business and need new furniture, you'll face this choice sooner or later.

A: Out of hours. Nobody sees the work, but it needs after-hours access to the building and each visit is shorter.
B: Phased during the day. It finishes quicker overall, but parts of the space are out of use while each zone is fitted.

Lots of businesses do a bit of both, with reception after hours and staff areas during the day. Which would work for you? Comment A or B and tell us what sort of business it is. Got a fit-out in mind? Get in touch here:
